 Smt. Bijaya @ Bijoya Paul
 Vs.
 The State of West Bengal & ors.
 Mr. Pradip Kumar Patra,
 Mr. S. Pal
 ...for the petitioner
 Mr. Biswabrata Basu Mallick, Ld. A.G.P.
 Mr. Sanjib Das
 ...for the State
 Mr. Suman Basu
 ...for the respondent no.3
Mr. Arup Kundu, Mr. Chittapriya Ghosh, Ms. Priyanka Saha ...for the respondent no.9

The writ
petition is directed against an order dated February 21, 2023 passed in O.A.257 of 2022.
By the impugned order, the Tribunal recorded that, the office of the Accountant General sought information for issuance of a fresh family pension payment order in favour of Jyotsna Pal.
The Tribunal disposed of the Original Application.
The petitioner claims herself to be the first wife of the deceased employee.
There is a dispute as to who was first wife of the deceased employee.
We called for the Service Book of the deceased employee.
Service Book of the deceased employee is produced in Court and perused.
The Service Book records that the petitioner before us is the wife of the deceased employee.
The private respondent no.9 before us claims that the private respondent is the first wife of the deceased employee on the basis of a marriage registration certificate.
The deceased employee during his lifetime filed a proceeding under Section 24 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 for dissolution of marriage with the respondent no.9 which was dismissed.

The private respondent also claims that,

sentences.text: she lodged a First Information Report against the deceased employee with regard to his subsequent marriage with the petitioner herein.
We perused the application under Section 24 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 being Matrimonial Suit No.36 of 14 filed before the learned Additional District and Sessions Judge, Khatra, Bankura.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Khatra, Bankura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Such application, speaks of the private respondent being married to another person on the date when the private respondent contracted marriage with the deceased employee.

It also goes on to say that there was a criminal case initiated by the private respondent against her earlier husband being Bindu @ Bindu Charan Mandal and his relatives under Sections 498A/323/494/506 of the Indian Penal Code before learned Judicial Magistrate, Khatra under Section 156(3) of the Criminal Procedure Code and Ranibandh Police Station F.I.R. No.40/91 corresponding to G.R.858/91 under Sections 498A/323/494/506 of the Indian Penal Code against Bindu @ Bindu Charan Mandal and his relatives were started on June 17, 1991.

There is a writing dated August 23, 2022 by which, the Sub Divisional Land and Land Reforms Officer, Khatra, Bankura opined that the private respondent is the first wife of the deceased employee.
State is represented.
State will produce records relating to the police case alluded to in this order.
State will also produce records on the basis of which the Sub Divisional Land and Land Reforms Officer, Khatra, Bankura made the observation as noted in the writing dated August 23, 2022.
No disbursement of family pension should made without the leave of the Court.
List the writ petition on July 26, 2023 when the documents as called for be produced.
Service Book produced is returned to the learned advocate for the Accountant General.

(Debangsu Basak, J.) (Md. Shabbar Rashidi, J.)
